a: Data verification refers to testing the integrity of the system. It has two methods, proofreading and double entry. Double entry is when the system keys in the data twice ✗ and compares the two values to see if they match. If they don't match an error is produced. Proofreading is when the user manually checks and compares their values by reading over it themselves to see if it is the intended value. Data verification is very effective as it tests the integrity of the system.
note: Quality of written communication assessed. Double entry is when a PERSON enters the data twice, not the system. To 'discuss effectiveness' you must say what verification can't do, e.g. it only checks that data has been copied correctly from the source, so if the source is wrong, the wrong data is still accepted.

a: Client side processing is when most of the processing that is needed for the system is carried out on the client's computer etc so that it doesn't slow down the server speed. Server side processing is then taking place near the end when the client has finished their side of the processing. In terms of this system client side will take place when entering their password / username and selecting items. Server side take place at the end authorising the payment.
note: Quality of written communication assessed; middle band. Uses the scenario but checking the username and password happens on the SERVER, not the client. Client-side example: checking all sections of the form are filled in. Server-side: login check, stock check, payment and the confirmation email.
